cards.front: Which proteins do the three main HIV genes (env, gag, pol) encode?
cards.back: **env**: gp160, cut into **gp120** (binds CD4 and the coreceptor) and **gp41** (membrane fusion). **gag**: **p24** capsid and p17 matrix. **pol**: **reverse transcriptase**, **integrase** and **protease**. The genome is two copies of (+) ssRNA.
cards.back_pt: **env**: gp160, clivada em **gp120** (liga-se ao CD4 e ao correceptor) e **gp41** (fusão de membranas). **gag**: capsídeo **p24** e matriz p17. **pol**: **transcriptase reversa**, **integrase** e **protease**. O genoma tem duas cópias de RNA fita simples (+).

cards.front: Why is an HIV antibody test not used to diagnose HIV in an infant born to an HIV-positive mother?
cards.back: **Maternal IgG crosses the placenta** and can stay in the infant's blood for up to about **18 months**, so an antibody test may be positive without infection. Infants are tested with a **nucleic acid test** (HIV RNA or DNA PCR).
cards.back_pt: A **IgG materna atravessa a placenta** e pode permanecer no sangue do lactente por até cerca de **18 meses**; assim, um teste de anticorpos pode ser positivo sem infecção. Lactentes são testados com **teste de ácido nucleico** (PCR para RNA ou DNA do HIV).

cards.front: Which HIV-related infections can appear before the CD4 count falls below 200/mm³?
cards.back: **Tuberculosis** and bacterial pneumonia can occur at **any CD4 count**. As CD4 falls below about **500/mm³**: **oral thrush**, **herpes zoster** and **oral hairy leukoplakia** (EBV). *Pneumocystis*, *Toxoplasma*, MAC and CMV come later, at lower counts.
cards.back_pt: **Tuberculose** e pneumonia bacteriana podem ocorrer com **qualquer contagem de CD4**. Quando o CD4 cai abaixo de cerca de **500/mm³**: **candidíase oral**, **herpes-zóster** e **leucoplasia pilosa oral** (EBV). *Pneumocystis*, *Toxoplasma*, MAC e CMV vêm depois, com contagens menores.

cards.front: What are the key genome rules for RNA viruses (strand, segments, polymerase)?
cards.back: Almost all are **single-stranded**; **reoviruses** (rotavirus) are **double-stranded**. **Negative-strand** viruses carry their own **RNA-dependent RNA polymerase**. Segmented genomes: **bunyaviruses, orthomyxoviruses, arenaviruses, reoviruses**; segments allow **reassortment**.
cards.back_pt: Quase todos são de **fita simples**; os **reovírus** (rotavírus) são de **fita dupla**. Vírus de **fita negativa** carregam sua própria **RNA polimerase dependente de RNA**. Genomas segmentados: **buniavírus, ortomixovírus, arenavírus, reovírus**; os segmentos permitem **rearranjo** (*reassortment*).

cards.front: How does antigenic drift differ from antigenic shift in influenza?
cards.back: **Drift**: small **point mutations** in hemagglutinin and neuraminidase genes; causes yearly **epidemics**. **Shift**: **reassortment** of genome segments between human and animal strains (influenza A only) creates a new HA or NA; can cause **pandemics**.
cards.back_pt: ***Drift*** (variação menor): pequenas **mutações pontuais** nos genes da hemaglutinina e da neuraminidase; causa **epidemias** anuais. ***Shift*** (variação maior): **rearranjo** de segmentos do genoma entre cepas humanas e animais (só influenza A) cria nova HA ou NA; pode causar **pandemias**.

cards.front: What are the classic features and late complication of measles (rubeola)?
cards.back: A paramyxovirus. Fever with **cough, coryza and conjunctivitis**, then **Koplik spots** (white spots on the buccal mucosa) before a rash that spreads **from the head downward**. Rare late complication: **subacute sclerosing panencephalitis** (SSPE) years later.
cards.back_pt: Um paramixovírus. Febre com **tosse, coriza e conjuntivite**, depois **manchas de Koplik** (pontos brancos na mucosa jugal) antes de um exantema que se espalha **da cabeça para baixo**. Complicação tardia rara: **panencefalite esclerosante subaguda** (PEES) anos depois.

cards.front: How do the diseases of Coxsackie A and Coxsackie B viruses differ?
cards.back: Both are picornaviruses (enteroviruses). **Coxsackie A**: **hand-foot-and-mouth disease** and **herpangina** (vesicles on the soft palate). **Coxsackie B**: **myocarditis**, **pericarditis** and **pleurodynia** (sudden chest wall pain). Both can cause aseptic meningitis.
cards.back_pt: Ambos são picornavírus (enterovírus). **Coxsackie A**: **doença mão-pé-boca** e **herpangina** (vesículas no palato mole). **Coxsackie B**: **miocardite**, **pericardite** e **pleurodinia** (dor súbita na parede torácica). Ambos podem causar meningite asséptica.

cards.front: How do the inactivated (Salk) and oral (Sabin) polio vaccines differ?
cards.back: **IPV** (Salk): killed virus given by injection; makes **serum IgG**; cannot cause polio. **OPV** (Sabin): live attenuated, oral; also makes **gut IgA**, so it blocks spread, but it can rarely revert and cause **vaccine-derived paralytic polio**.
cards.back_pt: **VIP** (Salk): vírus inativado injetável; produz **IgG sérica**; não pode causar poliomielite. **VOP** (Sabin): vírus vivo atenuado, oral; produz também **IgA intestinal**, bloqueando a transmissão, mas raramente pode reverter e causar **poliomielite paralítica derivada da vacina**.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has had fever, sore throat, muscle aches and a rash for 5 days. Three weeks ago he had condomless sex with a new partner. Temperature is 38.6°C. Exam shows painful oral ulcers, enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and axillae, and a pink macular rash on the trunk. A heterophile antibody test is negative. A fourth-generation HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay is reactive, but an HIV-1/HIV-2 antibody differentiation immunoassay is negative. Plasma HIV-1 RNA is very high. Which substance in his blood most likely made the screening test reactive?
choices: Proviral DNA in CD4+ T cells
questions.explanation: This is **acute HIV infection** (acute retroviral syndrome). In the first weeks, the virus replicates fast and **p24 capsid antigen** appears in the blood before antibodies form. A fourth-generation test detects both p24 and antibodies, so it turns positive earlier than antibody-only tests. The screen can also detect early IgM, but IgG antibodies to gp41 would make the differentiation assay positive, and it is still negative; the high HIV-1 RNA confirms the infection.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **infecção aguda pelo HIV** (síndrome retroviral aguda). Nas primeiras semanas, o vírus se replica rapidamente e o **antígeno p24 do capsídeo** aparece no sangue antes da formação de anticorpos. O teste de quarta geração detecta o p24 e os anticorpos, por isso fica positivo antes dos testes que detectam só anticorpos. A triagem também detecta IgM precoce, mas anticorpos IgG contra a gp41 tornariam positivo o imunoensaio de diferenciação, que ainda é negativo; o RNA do HIV-1 elevado confirma a infecção.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has had condomless sex for 8 years with her husband, who has untreated HIV infection and a high viral load. All of her HIV tests, including HIV-1 RNA, are negative. Her CD4+ T-cell count is normal, and she has never had unusual infections. The virus isolated from her husband infects macrophages but not T-cell lines in culture. In the laboratory, this virus binds to CD4 on her T cells but does not enter them. Lack of which host protein best explains her resistance?
questions.explanation: HIV **gp120** binds **CD4** first and then a **chemokine coreceptor**; this triggers **gp41**-mediated fusion. Macrophage-tropic (R5) strains, which cause most new infections, use **CCR5**. People homozygous for a deletion in the CCR5 gene (**CCR5-Δ32**) lack the coreceptor and are highly resistant to these strains. **CXCR4** is used by T-cell-tropic (X4) strains, which usually appear late; CD4 is present, because the virus binds her T cells and her CD4 count is normal.
questions.explanation_pt: A **gp120** do HIV liga-se primeiro ao **CD4** e depois a um **correceptor de quimiocina**; isso desencadeia a fusão mediada pela **gp41**. Cepas com tropismo por macrófagos (R5), que causam a maioria das novas infecções, usam o **CCR5**. Pessoas homozigotas para uma deleção no gene do CCR5 (**CCR5-Δ32**) não têm o correceptor e são muito resistentes a essas cepas. O **CXCR4** é usado por cepas com tropismo por linfócitos T (X4), que costumam surgir tardiamente; o CD4 está presente, pois o vírus se liga aos linfócitos T dela e a contagem de CD4 é normal.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has had a runny nose and low fever for 2 days. Tonight he developed a loud, barking cough, a hoarse voice, and a high-pitched noise when he breathes in, which gets worse when he cries. Temperature is 38.1°C, respiratory rate is 32/min, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. He is not drooling and does not look toxic. Lungs have no wheezes. An anteroposterior neck x-ray shows narrowing of the trachea just below the vocal cords. Which virus is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Barking cough, hoarseness, inspiratory **stridor** and subglottic narrowing (the ***steeple sign***) define **croup** (laryngotracheobronchitis). **Parainfluenza virus**, a paramyxovirus, is the most common cause. **RSV** is the most tempting choice, but it mainly causes **bronchiolitis** in infants, with wheezing and crackles from small-airway disease, not stridor. Influenza and adenovirus can cause croup less often, and measles would bring Koplik spots and a rash.
questions.explanation_pt: Tosse ladrante, rouquidão, **estridor** inspiratório e estreitamento subglótico (o ***steeple sign***, sinal da torre de igreja) definem o **crupe** (laringotraqueobronquite). O **vírus parainfluenza**, um paramixovírus, é a causa mais comum. O **VSR** é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas causa principalmente **bronquiolite** em lactentes, com sibilos e estertores por doença de pequenas vias aéreas, e não estridor. Influenza e adenovírus causam crupe com menor frequência, e o sarampo traria manchas de Koplik e exantema.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has had high fever for 4 days. She returned 1 week ago from a month of travel in Southeast Asia, where she had many mosquito bites. She has a severe headache behind the eyes and intense pain in her muscles and bones. Temperature is 39.4°C and blood pressure is 112/72 mm Hg. She has a diffuse red rash. Her joints are not swollen. After a blood pressure cuff is inflated on her arm to a pressure midway between systolic and diastolic for 5 minutes, many petechiae appear below it. Leukocyte count is 2,600/mm³, and platelet count is 62,000/mm³. Which virus is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Fever, **retro-orbital headache**, severe myalgia and bone pain, rash, a **positive tourniquet test**, **leukopenia** and **thrombocytopenia** point to **dengue**, a flavivirus spread by *Aedes* mosquitoes. **Chikungunya**, carried by the same mosquito, is the most tempting distractor, but it is dominated by severe, often swollen **polyarthritis**, and marked thrombocytopenia is less typical. Yellow fever causes **jaundice** and liver necrosis, and Zika is usually mild, with conjunctivitis.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre, **cefaleia retro-orbitária**, mialgia intensa e dor óssea, exantema, **prova do laço positiva**, **leucopenia** e **plaquetopenia** indicam **dengue**, um flavivírus transmitido por mosquitos *Aedes*. A **chikungunya**, transmitida pelo mesmo mosquito, é o distrator mais tentador, mas é dominada por **poliartrite** intensa, muitas vezes com edema articular, e plaquetopenia acentuada é menos típica. A febre amarela causa **icterícia** e necrose hepática, e a Zika costuma ser leve, com conjuntivite.

notes.title: RNA viruses and HIV: a high-yield map
notes.body_md:
## HIV

- **Retrovirus**: diploid (+) ssRNA; **reverse transcriptase** makes DNA, and **integrase** inserts it into the host genome.
- Entry: **gp120** binds **CD4**, then **CCR5** (early, R5 strains) or **CXCR4** (late, X4 strains); **gp41** drives fusion.
- Course: **acute** flu- or mono-like illness, then a long **clinical latency**, then **AIDS** (CD4 below 200/mm³ or an AIDS-defining illness).
- Screening: a **fourth-generation antigen/antibody** test (p24 plus antibodies), then an antibody differentiation assay; **HIV RNA** resolves early or unclear cases.
- Mother-to-child spread: in utero, at delivery, or by breastfeeding. Drug mechanisms: see the antimicrobial block.

## HTLV-1

- Retrovirus endemic in Japan, the Caribbean and Brazil; spreads by breastfeeding, sex and blood.
- Causes **adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma** (see leukemias) and **HTLV-1-associated myelopathy** (tropical spastic paraparesis).

## Respiratory

- **Influenza** (orthomyxovirus): **hemagglutinin** binds sialic acid; **neuraminidase** releases new virions.
- **RSV**: **bronchiolitis** in infants; **palivizumab** is a monoclonal antibody against its F protein.
- **Mumps**: **parotitis**, orchitis, aseptic meningitis.
- **Rubella** (matonavirus; older books: togavirus): mild rash with posterior auricular nodes; congenital rubella: see the TORCH notes.
- **SARS-CoV-2** (coronavirus): spike protein binds **ACE2**.

## Enteric

- **Rotavirus** (dsRNA reovirus) and **norovirus** (calicivirus): see GI infections.
- **Hepatitis A** (picornavirus) and **hepatitis E**: fecal-oral, no chronic infection; hepatitis E can be fulminant in **pregnancy**.
- **Poliovirus**: destroys **anterior horn cells**, causing asymmetric flaccid paralysis.
- **Hepatitis C** is a flavivirus; disease details are in the GI blocks.

## Arboviruses and zoonoses

- **Yellow fever**: jaundice, **Councilman bodies**. **Zika**: congenital microcephaly. **West Nile**: *Culex*, birds, encephalitis or flaccid paralysis.
- **Rabies** (rhabdovirus): **retrograde axonal transport** to the CNS; **Negri bodies**.
- **Ebola** (filovirus): hemorrhagic fever from contact with body fluids.
- **Hantavirus** (bunyavirus): rodent droppings; pulmonary syndrome.
- **Arenaviruses**: Lassa fever, lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus; rodent hosts.
notes.body_pt_md:
## HIV

- **Retrovírus**: RNA fita simples (+) diploide; a **transcriptase reversa** produz DNA, e a **integrase** o insere no genoma do hospedeiro.
- Entrada: a **gp120** liga-se ao **CD4** e depois ao **CCR5** (cepas R5, precoces) ou ao **CXCR4** (cepas X4, tardias); a **gp41** promove a fusão.
- Evolução: doença **aguda** semelhante a gripe ou mononucleose, depois longa **latência clínica**, depois **aids** (CD4 abaixo de 200/mm³ ou doença definidora de aids).
- Triagem: teste de **quarta geração antígeno/anticorpo** (p24 mais anticorpos), depois imunoensaio de diferenciação de anticorpos; o **RNA do HIV** esclarece casos precoces ou duvidosos.
- Transmissão vertical: intraútero, no parto ou pela amamentação. Mecanismos dos fármacos: ver o bloco de antimicrobianos.

## HTLV-1

- Retrovírus endêmico no Japão, no Caribe e no Brasil; transmitido por amamentação, sexo e sangue.
- Causa **leucemia/linfoma de células T do adulto** (ver leucemias) e **mielopatia associada ao HTLV-1** (paraparesia espástica tropical).

## Respiratórios

- **Influenza** (ortomixovírus): a **hemaglutinina** liga-se ao ácido siálico; a **neuraminidase** libera os novos vírions.
- **VSR**: **bronquiolite** em lactentes; o **palivizumabe** é um anticorpo monoclonal contra sua proteína F.
- **Caxumba**: **parotidite**, orquite, meningite asséptica.
- **Rubéola** (matonavírus; livros mais antigos: togavírus): exantema leve com linfonodos retroauriculares; rubéola congênita: ver as notas de TORCH.
- **SARS-CoV-2** (coronavírus): a proteína *spike* liga-se à **ECA2**.

## Entéricos

- **Rotavírus** (reovírus de RNA fita dupla) e **norovírus** (calicivírus): ver infecções gastrointestinais.
- **Hepatite A** (picornavírus) e **hepatite E**: transmissão fecal-oral, sem infecção crônica; a hepatite E pode ser fulminante na **gestação**.
- **Poliovírus**: destrói os **neurônios do corno anterior**, causando paralisia flácida assimétrica.
- A **hepatite C** é um flavivírus; detalhes da doença estão nos blocos de GI.

## Arbovírus e zoonoses

- **Febre amarela**: icterícia, **corpúsculos de Councilman**. **Zika**: microcefalia congênita. **Febre do Nilo Ocidental**: *Culex*, aves, encefalite ou paralisia flácida.
- **Raiva** (rabdovírus): **transporte axonal retrógrado** até o SNC; **corpúsculos de Negri**.
- **Ebola** (filovírus): febre hemorrágica por contato com fluidos corporais.
- **Hantavírus** (buniavírus): excretas de roedores; síndrome pulmonar.
- **Arenavírus**: febre de Lassa, vírus da coriomeningite linfocitária; hospedeiros roedores.
